newsitem.title: UK: BCC sees some sign of UK service sector inflation.
newsitem.headline: BCC sees some sign of UK service sector inflation.

text.p: The British Chambers of Commerce said its second quarter survey showed some signs of service sector inflation with a positive balance of 21 percent of companies forecasting price rises over the next three months.
That stood in stark contrast to manufacturing firms covered in the survey where only a balance of 8.0 percent expected prices to rise.
The BCC said policy-makers faced a dilemma in curbing those inflationary pressures without further damaging manufacturing exports.
"It may be necessary for interest rates to rise further although we are certainly nor advocating it," said Ian Peters, BCC deputy director general.

He said the Bank of England's monetary policy committee must pay close attention to the concerns of exporters and said there was a case to be made for greater business representation on the committee.
"But we're not making a big deal about that we will have to judge the MPC by its actions."

Ian Fletcher, policy executive at the BCC, said fiscal measures introduced in Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown's first budget but not taking effect until next year could be the last thing the economy needs by then if there has already been a succession of rate rises.

Peters said the budget had been a missed opportunity but said the Chancellor could still promote saving not spending of windfall payments by bringing forwards savings incentives he announced in his budget or at least announcing that they would be back dated when introduced next year.
